messages:
jordan (eng-infra): Heads-up: planning a preemptive NIC latency sweep in az7 next Tue 02:00-06:00 UTC. We'll do a staged node reboot/drain across the GPU pools to validate NIC firmware fixes. Expected impact: brief per-node eviction (1-3m) + degraded capacity during waves. No API-wide outage expected.
ash (eng-sre): +1. Can you post exact batches and backfill policy? I want to check the autoscaler thresholds.
jordan (eng-infra): Plan: 6 waves, 10 nodes per wave from pool-gpu-large (priority) then pool-gpu-small. Wave cadence 20m between waves, 02:00 start. Backfill: allow spot backfill up to 15% during each wave, otherwise route to eu/na spare capacity. If we see >5% request errors, we pause and fallback routes trigger.
marie (eng-runtime): Add KV cache warmup after each wave — otherwise tail latency spikes for long-context chat. I'll add a post-drain job to pre-warm prefixes.
teo (oncall): @jordan please include the exact node label selector so I can run a quick smoke before each wave. Also my oncall window overlaps, I'll be watching logs.
jordan (eng-infra): selector: "node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=az7-preemptive-sweep". Smoke test: curl /health on the local sidecar + run `rts latency-check --sample 200 --max-rt 120` (ms). If >120ms, abort wave. I pushed a runbook to /runbooks/az7-nic-sweep (link: https://internal/redwood/runbooks/az7-nic-sweep).
ash (eng-sre): Thanks. Ops-bot, can you schedule the waves and post reminders 10m before each wave?
ops-bot: Scheduled 6 maintenance windows starting at 02:00 UTC on Tue Mar 24. Reminders set for 10m and 1m before each wave. Maintenance ID: MNT-az7-20260324-01.
sam (product): FYI customer-facing note: Dedicated customers in eu/na shouldn't be impacted, but we may surface a transient capacity metric in Console. Recommend adding a one-liner to status when we start the first wave.
marie (eng-runtime): I'll flip on extra sampling for canary routes and capture traces from 02:00-07:00 for regression analysis. If we hit model fallbacks we need to correlate with kv-warm metrics.
nash (eng-sre): Quick cost check — if we route to spare capacity in eu/na, estimated incremental GPU-hours ~ 12h peak across the window, approx $2.7k. Approve?
jordan (eng-infra): Approved for this sweep; we've budgeted for emergency backfill. Keep me posted on cost spikes.
teo (oncall): I'll run a preflight at 01:30: `node-exporter` health, `etcd` latency <10ms, and netpol checks. If anything fails I'll raise a hold in this thread.
jordan (eng-infra): Action items: 1) ash: confirm autoscaler thresholds for spot backfill 2) marie: post-drain kv warm job 3) teo: preflight + smoke 01:30 4) ops-bot: reminders + maintenance page update 5) sam: publish status blurb at wave-0 start. We'll monitor latency, error rate, and token generation QPS.
nash (eng-sre): I'll adjust autoscaler to allow 15% backfill with cooldown 300s, and set a fail-open if errors >5% sustained for 3m.
marie (eng-runtime): Post-drain warm command (example):
```bash
kubectl label nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=az7-preemptive-sweep example=warmup
kubectl run kv-warm --image=redwood/kv-warm:stable --replicas=5 -- /app/warm --prefixes-file /config/prefixes.txt
```
ops-bot: Reminder 10m until wave 1 (02:00 UTC).
teo (oncall): Preflight done 01:30: all green except one node with high tx_errors, ticket #INF-4492 created. That node removed from wave selection.
jordan (eng-infra): Good catch. Removing node INF-4492 from selector. Proceeding with wave 1. I'll post immediate updates in this thread.
ops-bot: Wave 1 started: cordon+drain 10 nodes. ETA per node ~3m.
nash (eng-sre): Watching autoscaler behavior. No error spike so far.
marie (eng-runtime): KV warm completed after wave 1, tail latency steady.
teo (oncall): Wave 1 done. No regressions. Proceeding to wave 2 in 20m.
sam (product): Posted status: "Planned maintenance in az7; transient capacity impact being mitigated by routing. We expect brief per-node evictions. Monitoring closely." :thumbsup:
jordan (eng-infra): Thanks team — will update when all waves complete or if we hit hold.
